title: Could AI improve work while weakening our ability to evaluate it? A P&G field study
discussion_signal: The public translation describes a field study of hundreds of P&G commercial and R&D professionals: AI improved idea quality and helped individuals work beyond their functional expertise, but AI users were less accurate at selecting their strongest idea. The discussion therefore separates output quality from evaluative judgment and learning.
linked_research_question: When AI improves product-innovation output and cross-functional balance, what happens to judgment, expertise sharing, social engagement, and the ability to recognize weak or strong ideas?
limits: The field experiment is in one consumer-goods firm and one bounded innovation task
The public post reports selected results rather than the full design and estimates
Higher output quality does not establish durable learning, organizational adoption, or consumer-market success
